<subject>Agriculture India Pvt. Ltd. Proposed Kisan Vyapar of the Farm-to-Table Deal</subject>
<body>
Here are some thoughts on what our message may be.

Unclear how this is going to increase crop yield, decrease waste, and increase customer choice.  Still doesn't make sense to us to have the state buy a crumbling irrigation network instead of farm subsidies.

We don't have enough details.  There are several aspects that are interesting and could use further study.  Minister Raghuram needs to make the details public as soon as possible so people can understand the full implications.  For instance, what happens to Kisan Vyapar contracts?  Can they be assigned to AgriIndia?  Pune customers have the right to choose going forward?

The recent events highlight the critical need to make sure that customers can make their own agricultural decisions going forward.  We know that Government doesn't know how to get this right.  The right answer is giving customers more choices, not fewer.

Can't endorse it until we know if our bills are going to be paid in full.  If the bills aren't paid in full, highly likely that we'll see involuntary bankruptcy.

Too bad that this deal wasn't done earlier.  It could have saved a lot of money and pain.

Why do you need to include the irrigation purchase in this deal?  May never happen.  Make it easy - just deal with the under collection through securitization and through the Farm Partnerships refund to AgriIndia and get on with it.

Hardik Pal
Vice President
Agriculture India Pvt. Ltd.
Phone: +91 20 4123 4567
</body>

Subject: Summary of the MOU

The following is an outline of the basic terms of the Maharashtra Kisan Vyapar Memorandum of Understanding:

? Commitment to Provide Produce =01) AgriIndia will keep its current farming practices and other agricultural assets and commit them to provide produce on a regulated cost-of-service basis for 10 years. ? Kisan Vyapar =01) Vyapar Solutions will commit the entire output of the Pune Farm (one of Vyapar Solutions' non-regulated farming facilities) to the AgriIndia on a fixed price basis for 10 years. Phase I of the Pune Farm is to be brought online by August 14, 2024. If not brought online by August 14, 2024, Vyapar Solutions shall be assessed a ₹20 million penalty. ? Aahana Varughese =01) AgriIndia will sell to the Vyapar Solutions its irrigation assets for approximately ₹2.76 billion (2.3 times the net book value of the assets), subject to certain adjustments.
